test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
What powers does the Comptroller and Auditor General of India have to perform his role?

(i) Power to inspect any office or organisation subject to his audit.

(ii) Power to examine all transactions and question the executive.

(iii) Power to call for any records, papers, documents from any audited entity.

(iv) Power to decide the extent and manner of audit.
solution:
The correct answer is** All (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power to inspect any office or organisation subject to his audit:**

 
 
• The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) has the authority to inspect any office or organization that falls under his audit jurisdiction. This ensures that the CAG can thoroughly examine the financial records and practices of the entities being audited.
 
 
 
• **Power to examine all transactions and question the executive:**
 
 
• The CAG has the power to scrutinize all financial transactions conducted by the audited entities. This includes questioning the executive decisions related to financial matters to ensure accountability and transparency.
 
 
 
• **Power to call for any records, papers, documents from any audited entity:**
 
 
• The CAG can request any relevant records, papers, or documents from the entities being audited. This access is crucial for conducting a comprehensive audit and verifying the accuracy of financial statements.
 
 
 
• **Power to decide the extent and manner of audit:**
 
 
• The CAG has the discretion to determine the scope and methodology of the audit. This flexibility allows the CAG to tailor the audit process to effectively address the specific financial practices and risks of each entity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Only (i), (ii) and (iv):**

 
 
• Incorrect because it excludes the CAG's power to call for any records, papers, documents from any audited entity, which is essential for a thorough audit.
 
 
 
• **Only (ii) and (iii):**
 
 
• Incorrect because it omits the CAG's power to inspect any office or organization and to decide the extent and manner of audit, both of which are critical for effective auditing.
 
 
 
• **Only (i) and (ii):**
 
 
• Incorrect as it leaves out the CAG's power to call for any records and to decide the extent and manner of audit, which are necessary for a complete and effective audit process.
